summary: Shows making module parameters optional with default(omit), so Ansible doesn't send the parameter (e.g. mode falls back to umask). When chaining filters, use default(None) | some_filter or omit.
questions: How do I skip a module parameter when a variable isn't set?
What does omit do in Ansible?
How do I set file mode only for some items in a loop?
How do I use omit when chaining other filters?

answer_card.title: Making parameters optional with omit
answer_card.answer_md:
```yaml
- ansible.builtin.file:
    dest: "{{ item.path }}"
    state: touch
    mode: "{{ item.mode | default(omit) }}"
  loop:
    - path: /tmp/foo
    - path: /tmp/baz
      mode: "0444"
```

Where `mode` is missing, it isn't sent at all (the system umask applies).

If you chain filters after it, use `"{{ foo | default(None) | some_filter or omit }}"`. This depends on how the later filters handle `None`, so expect some trial and error.
